subject: penguin
pitch: An emperor penguin chick's proud parent. Glossy blue-black back and head, a crisp white belly blending into a warm golden-yellow patch at the neck and ear, a long slender beak with an orange-pink stripe, stubby flippers held slightly out, and big black feet. A fluffy grey chick peeks out from between its feet.
reasoning:
I'm sketching out the proportions for the scene: an adult emperor penguin around 1.1 meters tall standing at the origin, with a smaller fluffy grey chick positioned between its feet, peeking out at a reduced scale.

I'm planning the API surface I'll use conservatively—joints, chains, sweeps, parts, surface placement, and paint functions—then mapping out the penguin's skeleton starting with a hip root joint for the upright body.

For the legs and feet, I'm working out how to orient extruded webbed foot shapes flat against the floor with toes pointing forward, calculating the local axis directions so the thickness runs vertically while the outline spans the foot's footprint, then sketching the toe points for the outline.

For the legs themselves, since they're mostly hidden under the body, I'm planning to build them as simple joint chains from hip to ankle, considering whether to use a two-point chain or add a hidden knee joint for better structure.

Now I'm sketching the overall penguin rig structure—an upright torso built as a swept egg-like shape along a catmull spine path, with a hips root joint, spine chain, and a neck leading up to a head joint, all parented hierarchically.

For the body sweep I'm defining a tapering radius profile (narrower at belly, wider mid-body, narrower near the neck) bound to the spine/hips chain, and planning the black-and-white coloring with a darker back and white belly.

For coloring I'm using normal-based paint logic: surfaces facing upward become dark blue-black, the forward-facing belly region becomes white, and I'm adding a golden patch near the neck/ears based on position and normal direction, with a touch of noise to make the edges look natural rather than perfectly sharp.

Now I'm figuring out the head: a sphere attached to the head bone positioned near the model's top, keeping it dark to match the emperor penguin's coloring, then working out how to place the yellow ear patch as a small surface decal oriented around the head using angular positioning.

I'm deciding to add the gold patch via a paint function on the head sphere instead, using normal-vector conditions to shade the ear and neck regions appropriately, then moving to the beak—sweeping a tapered tube from the head's front toward a tip point, planning to paint stripe patterns along its length for the characteristic dark-to-orange coloring.

Then I'm considering adding a separate jaw joint near the head front to support building the upper and lower mandibles independently.

For the eyes, I'm planning small dark spheres positioned symmetrically on the sides of the head. For the flippers, I'm sketching stubby, flattened limbs curving down from the shoulders, using a tapering radius profile so they read as flat plates held slightly away from the body.

Still working out flipper orientation...

Working out the naming convention for joint chains: a path with three points needs three names since the span count plus one tip joint determines it, so I'll settle on ["shoulderL","elbowL","handL"] for the flipper arm chain, and wire the extrude's bone parameter to reference the first joint of that chain.

I'm positioning the flipper paddle relative to the elbow joint, computing its origin point along the arm chain around the midpoint, and adjusting the outline's vertical span so it stretches from shoulder-height down toward the hand while rigidly attaching to the elbow bone.

Now I'm working on the legs, defining a short catmull chain for each hidden leg, sweeping a thin black rod along it, then shaping webbed feet as flat extruded outlines in the XZ plane—positioning each foot's thickness just above the floor and sketching a rounded heel with a sharp pointed toe at the front.

Attaching the foot shape at the ankle joint so it extends forward from the leg tip, I then turn to the chick: a fluffy grey blob sitting between the parent's feet, with a smaller head sphere, tiny beak, and eye added on top.

I decide to keep it simple rather than building true feathery texture with cards or spikes, just using layered spheres for fluff. For positioning, I'll let the chick's parts attach to the nearest joint (likely the hips) rather than creating a dedicated chick joint, and I need to place it at roughly x=0, low to the ground, peeking out between the feet without clipping into the parent's belly.

For the chick's body shape, I'm considering a sphere versus a swept capsule, but settling on simple spheres for body and head, then scattering small puff spheres across the surface to simulate fuzzy down.

I'm also adding tiny details like the beak and eyes, and thinking through how foot placement interacts with the ground plane -- the lowest points need to touch or sink slightly into the floor rather than float above it.

For the body structure, I'm setting up a spine chain from the hips rising through two joints to roughly 0.95m, then continuing into the neck and head joints to build out the rest of the rig.

Still defining the rig joints...

I'll simplify to a scalar radius taper rather than ellipse pairs, since the body's width-depth difference is small enough to ignore. I'm adjusting where the torso bottom sits relative to the legs and floor, settling on a path from y=0.3 to 1.0 with radii tapering from 0.08 at the base up to 0.15 at mid-body and back down to 0.11 near the neck, leaving the legs visible below.

I'm placing hip joints inside the body and defining a three-point leg chain (hip, knee, ankle) with two spans of names plus a tip, mirroring left/right using a sign-based side label. For the flippers, I'm setting up a three-point arm chain parented to a spine joint, and starting on the paddle extrusion shape for the flipper geometry.

Working out flipper outline and orientation...

Now I'm setting up the color palette (ink, white, gold, orange-pink, beak, foot, greys, eye) and figuring out the paint logic for the body: using noise to create a ragged white belly boundary based on front-facing normals and height, then adding a golden neck/ear patch where the normal points sideways and y is high enough.

I'm checking that `paint` and `noise` are imported correctly from the module, then moving to defining the head paint callback with a similar gold ear-patch rule based on normal direction and vertical position near the eye joints.

Now I'm computing the head sphere geometry and placement, realizing the eye spheres I placed by raw coordinates actually float outside the head surface, so I switch to using a surface-projection helper that places eyes relative to the head center using azimuth and elevation angles instead.

Then I work out the beak as a bezier sweep embedded into the head front, tapering from a wider base to a slender tip, with a tapering radius function, and start planning an orange-pink stripe accent along the lower mandible side.

I'm adding a jaw joint parented to the head that aims toward the beak tip, and sweeping a shorter lower mandible bezier with its own tapering radius, keeping it colored to match the beak with the orange stripe detail.

For the chick, I'm positioning a small body and head sphere nestled against the parent penguin's body so it reads as peeking out between the legs, checking that the overlaps look natural rather than clipping oddly. I'm also planning to scatter fluff details across the chick's body sphere for texture.

I realize the chick's nearest joint lookup might snap to a leg or ankle bone instead of the hips due to proximity, so I'll explicitly pass the hips bone when placing the chick parts and its fluff stickers to keep everything rigidly attached where intended.

For the beak, I'm using a small spike geometry tapering to a tip near the head front, colored orange, anchored to the hips bone. The eyes get placed similarly using small dark surface hits on the chick head.

Now I'm working out the feet geometry — a dark extruded outline positioned slightly off-center and forward, computing the correct thickness axis so the foot shape extrudes properly along the ground plane.

Legs get built as tapered tube sweeps directly from the leg bone chain, using a dark foot color and a radius that narrows from the top to the ankle, while I'm making sure the body sweep uses a separate catmull path across spine bones to properly close out the bottom silhouette.

I'm checking that nothing clips through the ground or body — feet sit at zero, flipper tips stay around 0.59, and the leg-top joints stay hidden inside the body radius at that height. I'm also deciding to skip a tail detail for simplicity, confirming the spine chain's joint ownership over the body path segments, and placing the head joint just above the spine tip with a slight forward tilt so the head sphere sits flush against the top of the body without gapping.

Now I'm verifying API usage — surface() accepts a Part, paint() callbacks get used correctly in sweep color options, noise() takes a position and size, and scatter() uses a seeded rng with minimum distance spacing. I'm also making sure unused paint callback parameters get prefixed with underscores to satisfy the linter, like in the beak paint function, while leaving the body and head paint callbacks alone since they actually use their p and n arguments.

Now I'm setting up the module structure: importing from the builder library, defining a color palette as constants, exporting meta info, and starting the build function with a root hip joint and a spine chain built from catmull-rom control points. Writing penguin skeleton structure...

Writing coat paint logic...

Then I'm placing the head geometry at the bone position, adding eye stickers found by surface-hit lookups on either side of the face, and sculpting the beak as a bezier sweep with a tapering radius function and orange/beak color paint based on position.

Next I work out the lower mandible as a similar bezier sweep rooted at the jaw bone, then move on to building the flipper arms—defining a chain of shoulder/elbow/hand joints per side via catmull curve, and extruding a flipper outline along each arm bone with bevel and ink coloring.

For typing cleanliness, I'd pull the outline array out and explicitly annotate it as OutlinePoint[] so the "sharp" literal doesn't widen to a generic string. Now I'm starting the leg rig—another chain of hip/knee/ankle joints parented to the hips, with a sweep defining the leg's thickness and color.

Now I'm working through the feet, attaching an extruded foot shape to the ankle joint, oriented forward along the leg's local axes. Then I'm building the chick companion—body and head spheres parented at the hips, scattered fluff spheres across its surface using a seeded RNG for small sphere "fuzz," plus eyes and a small cone beak aimed forward.

I'm double-checking that all imports (rng, bezier, catmull, noise, paint, OutlinePoint) are used correctly, parent/joint relationships are consistent, and the geometry proportions (body radius, leg length, foot placement) keep the model grounded and visually balanced before finalizing the code.
